title: Min-Cut Isolation and Residual Reachability Invariants in a Swift Graph Topology Engine
topic: I shut down the L train in a FalkorDB graph: 23,445 riders, one min cut, and a fix tested
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: This paper investigates the algorithmic mechanics of isolating a critical subgraph within a directed network using a Swift-based max-flow engine. We model a transit network with 23,445 riders as a directed graph where edge capacities represent throughput limits. By implementing the Edmonds-Karp algorithm, we compute the maximum flow and identify the minimum cut that effectively "shuts down" a specific train line. We establish formal invariants regarding residual graph reachability and flow conservation. Static Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) analysis verifies the structural complexity of the implementation, confirming $O(|V| + |E|)$ traversal bounds and $O(|V| \cdot |E|^2)$ worst-case flow computation. We prove that the min-cut edges correspond exactly to the saturated forward edges crossing the residual reachable set. This work provides a reproducible, formally verified Swift implementation for network isolation tasks, demonstrating that min-cut identification is a direct consequence of max-flow computation without additional heuristic search. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/swift-systems-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261025_190139_i_shut_down_the_l_train_in_a_f}.
